title: Colette's birth chart
metaDescription: Colette's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 8.7° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Mercury holds a sextile to Venus at 0.9° — close enough to weld thinking to taste. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 8.7° of Aquarius is the Sun's exact seat — first decan, 0°–10°, sub-ruled by Saturn in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Capricorn (22.6°), Venus in Pisces (23.5°), Mars in Scorpio (2.5°): thought with its feet on the ground, attraction that works by atmosphere, effort that surges when it matters.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Mercury a sixth of the circle apart from Venus, 0.9° off exact. A sextile pays out only on effort; the scheme calls it opportunity rather than gift. Behind it, Mercury square Neptune at 1.1°, and Mars square Uranus at 1.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Sun opposes Uranus while both square Mars. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags four placements in this chart. The Sun in Aquarius at 8.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Pisces at 23.5° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Scorpio at 2.5° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Capricorn at 25.4° is in domicile. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: earth 3, fire 3, water 2, air 1 across the elements, and fixed 5, cardinal 3, mutable 1 across the modalities. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. Jupiter, Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Capricorn into Aquarius during that day at the birthplace, travelling 15.3° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
